title: Dish Preparation Dependencies
statement:
A kitchen has to prepare `n` items numbered `0` to `n - 1`: raw ingredients and intermediate preparations that are combined into a dish. You are given `m` dependencies. Each dependency is a pair `x y`, meaning item `x` cannot be prepared until item `y` has already been prepared.

An item that appears in no dependency as the first value can be prepared at any time. Once an item has been prepared it stays available, so it can be a prerequisite of any number of other items.

Decide whether it is possible to prepare **all** `n` items one after another in some order that respects every dependency. Print `true` if it is possible and `false` otherwise.

Dependencies may be repeated, and a dependency may even name the same item twice (`x x`), which can never be satisfied.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `m`.
Each of the next `m` lines contains two integers `x` and `y`: item `x` requires item `y` to be prepared first.
outputFormat: Print `true` if all items can be prepared, otherwise `false`.

examples.explanation: Item 0 needs items 1 and 2, and item 3 needs item 0. Preparing them in the order 1, 2, 0, 3 satisfies every dependency.
Item 1 needs 0 and 3, item 3 needs 2, and item 2 needs 1. So 1 waits for 3, 3 waits for 2 and 2 waits for 1: a circular dependency. Items 0 and 4 are fine, but not all items can be prepared.
Item 1 would have to be prepared before itself.

hints: Treat each item as a node and each dependency as a directed edge from the required item to the item that needs it.
All items can be prepared exactly when this graph has no directed cycle.
Repeatedly prepare an item whose remaining requirement count is zero (Kahn's algorithm). If you manage to prepare all n items there is no cycle; otherwise some items are stuck in a cycle.

def gen(rng):
    def fmt(n, es):
        return f"{n} {len(es)}\n" + "\n".join(f"{x} {y}" for x, y in es)

    def dag(n, m, relabel=True):
        order = list(range(n))
        rng.shuffle(order)
        es = []
        for _ in range(m):
            a, b = rng.sample(range(n), 2) if n > 1 else (0, 0)
            if a == b:
                continue
            if a < b:
                a, b = b, a
            es.append((order[a], order[b]))
        return es

    tests = [fmt(1, []), fmt(1, [(0, 0)]), fmt(2, [(0, 1), (1, 0)]), fmt(3, [(0, 1), (0, 1), (0, 1)]), fmt(4, [])]
    for n in (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7):
        for _ in range(3):
            tests.append(fmt(n, dag(n, rng.randint(0, 8))))
        for _ in range(3):
            es = dag(n, rng.randint(0, 6))
            es.append((rng.randrange(n), rng.randrange(n)))
            tests.append(fmt(n, es))
        for _ in range(2):
            es = [(rng.randrange(n), rng.randrange(n)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 7))]
            tests.append(fmt(n, es))
    N = 100000
    perm = list(range(N))
    rng.shuffle(perm)
    chain = [(perm[i], perm[i - 1]) for i in range(1, N)]
    tests.append(fmt(N, chain))
    bad = chain + [(perm[0], perm[N - 1])]
    tests.append(fmt(N, bad))
    tests.append(fmt(N, dag(N, 100000)))
    es = dag(N, 99999)
    es.append((perm[5], perm[N - 5]))
    es.append((perm[N - 5], perm[5]))
    tests.append(fmt(N, es[:100000]))
    tests.append(fmt(50000, dag(50000, 100000)))
    return tests
